authorial_core.interpreted_intent: The current request continues the actual prior user request for three independent reference-guided espionage photo tests. General knowledge resolves espionage as a photographic dramatic situation of information and observation, not evidence of any real identity or history. Random draw C selects a contact-sheet/window comparison: an observer, physical representations and the actual courtyard remain distinct. All dossier layout, hand positions, setting, timing, clothes and camera choices are replaceable authorial choices at creativity 1. A visitor should feel the tension between what a record depicts and what can currently be seen, without the photograph claiming that either is true, secret, causal, or from a proved date. Sensual 1 is subtle attentive presence and soft facial light; fetish 0 and surreal 0 add no treatment.
authorial_core.subject: A portrait-guided woman in a fictional espionage photograph
authorial_core.setting: Authorial records room and courtyard window
authorial_core.event: An authorial comparison of paper photographic records and a currently visible courtyard
visual_priorities: Portrait-guided observer, paper image and actual exterior occupy legibly separate planes.
Visible paper edges, contact-sheet gutters and clips distinguish the record carrier from the world it depicts.
The observer hand contacts the supported sheet while her gaze connects her to the window.
Repeated iron-gate geometry invites comparison while the window sill limits the actual field of view.
authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: A cinematic photographic espionage scene in a small records room beside a tall courtyard window. The portrait-guided woman compares physical photographic records with the space outside. Use the supplied portrait as facial and hair appearance guidance: a dark chin-length bob with fine separated bangs, the same facial proportions and natural features. She sits sideways at a wooden table in a charcoal cardigan over a pale open-collar shirt, her quiet appeal carried by attentive eyes and the soft window light on her cheek. An open dossier lies close to her on the tabletop. Its right page holds one large black-and-white contact sheet with four rectangular exposures separated by white gutters; the sheet has visible paper edges and two metal clips fastening it to the dossier page. The exposures show a courtyard with a distinctive iron gate and its diagonal crossbar. Her left fingertips rest on the lower white margin of the contact sheet, attached to a relaxed wrist and forearm supported by the table. Her right hand rests beside the closed cover. She has just raised her gaze from the records toward the courtyard. Through the window, the actual iron gate and diagonal crossbar stand beyond a real sill and the thickness of the wall; the visible courtyard is wet and still. A diagonal medium-wide view from the table corner holds her face, the paper sheet and the actual window opening together. The dossier occupies the lower foreground at a readable angle, her face the middle plane, and the cool courtyard the deeper right side. A small warm desk lamp separates the paper from the colder daylight; moderate depth of field keeps the sheet's image grid and the courtyard gate recognizable. Tactile paper, worn wood, soft skin texture and restrained colors create a tense moment of comparison.
